fixtures.text: The software may point out matching evidence and missing information. Someone with the proper permission still chooses whether to act.
The tool offers guidance; it does not get to make or carry out consequential choices on its own.
The software summarizes the agreement and lists the information it received.
The software might be able to pick the reviewer if the parties do not object.
A separate process handles most important actions, although the software handles the final step.
If a deadline is missed, the software can refund the money by itself.
The software may turn its recommendation into a binding result without asking anyone else.
The software can recommend a payment, while a different authorized process checks permission and decides whether to send it.
A required person reviews disputes, and the software appoints that person.
No confidence score lets the software replace a person's judgment, skip a control, or move money.
